# Zero health penetration testing 

**Name:** Obonguko Mfoniso Ubon  
ID: CSF/API/25B/1056  
Date: Feb 9, 2026

## Executive summary

This assessment evaluated the Zero-Health API through reconnaissance, authorization testing, and injection analysis. The passive and active reconnaissance tests, using Swagger files and captured network traffic, helped locate the main authentication, user, and role-based access endpoints. This informed which targeted endpoints would be tested, beginning with the login endpoint, which was the most critical.  
The BOLA test was successful because a normal user was not able to read, modify, or delete other users' records by altering the IDs or tokens of the objects being accessed, and the non-admin token did not grant access to sensitive information.  
Injection testing revealed a time-based SQL injection at login, in which the injection causes a delay in the application's response. This indicates the application does not sufficiently ensure safe queries are executed and could be vulnerable to unauthorized access and privilege escalation if not mitigated by parameterized queries.

## Key Findings 

**Reconnaissance** 

In the active reconnaissance phase, I manually attacked the API by sending some test requests and observing the responses. I discovered the different endpoints of the API, such as authentication, users, and role-based restrictions, by analyzing the status codes, response times, and error messages of the requests.

As part of passive reconnaissance, I reviewed public-facing sites like the project GitHub repo, api documentation, and developer tools to better understand how the API was structured, what parameters were taken, and how users authenticated.

With this information, I was now able to focus my attack on the more valuable endpoints, such as the login path, and determine which parameters I could inject and where I could land my successful authentication bypass (and thus pharmacist-level access).

**BOLA**

In my testing, I wasn't able to use a normal user's authentication token to view other users' information, no matter the endpoint I switched to, and despite the fact that I tried manipulating the tokens to carry out this attack, it didn't yield any positive results. 

I was able to view everyone’s result only using an admins token.  
![][image12]

---
